issues.claim: Partly fixed. The pipeline repair now gives the moat one water level, derived from its `flowFrom` source (§4.2 S3 (10): 'the source's surface at its shore point nearest the moat … which every reader of the moat's water reads (§8.4's water at its level, V04 §3.2 N2 and N7, §2.6's water table)'), and carves a wet stretch only where the ground stands 0 to `moat.maxFallCm` (400 cm) above that level. But §2.6's water table, one of the named readers, still reads 'the nearest water body's surface elevation (its shore's terrain sample)'. For a carved moat that sample is the bank top, up to 4 m above the derived level. So two base homes give two values for one water surface. A plot beside a wet moat on a slope reads a water table up to 4 m too high, and its cellar or crypt takes the half-sunk or crawl-space rung where a full one is lawful. That is a silent wrong result at the moat × slope edge EP-22 names. (V04 N7's own wording is VEW-r1-07.)
issues.required_change: §2.6, the water-table sentence: 'The water table is the nearest water body's surface elevation — a moat's the one level §4.2 S3 (10) derives from its `flowFrom` source, every other body's shore terrain sample — plus the freeboard …'. Add to EP-22's hill-town fixture (§4.13; B-EDGE): 'a plot within `waterTableM` of a wet moat reads the derived level + `freeboardCm` as its water table'.

issues.claim: Partly fixed. II.7.2 now reads as V04 §3.2 N2 and F-NET: no frame outfall, and a moat outfall, then a field outfall, where no water outfall is admitted. It closes on 'V04's T-V4-2 no-water fixture names the case'. T-V4-2 (V04 §7) is a stage invariant over the seed sets and names no fixture. The pipeline repair's hand-off ('V04: T-V4-2's no-water fixture names the field outfall (VEW-07)') was not applied. So the base points at a test fixture that does not exist. The plain dry site — no river, lake, sea, canal or oasis, and `moat: 'none'` — is tested only indirectly, through T-V4-80 (e)'s oasis town and (j)'s per-bank river towns.
issues.required_change: V04 §7, T-V4-2: append 'on a no-water fixture (a TOWN and a CITY with no river, lake, sea, canal or oasis, `moat: 'none'`): every run reaches the one field outfall beyond the outermost enceinte's outer strip, `requestedVsBuilt` naming the cess field, 0 `frame` outfalls'. II.7.2's pointer then resolves as written.

issues.claim: Two round-1 repairs disagree at the steepest site (VEW-03 × VEW-10). §4.2 S3 (9), *Every arc closed* (a mesa town, an island town filling its island): 'the stage walls nothing … its routes (5), picked by the land law on the whole contour as an unwalled town's are, enter across the barriers'. §4.3's new *class grade limit* makes 'an edge steeper than the routed class's grade limit … impassable to that route'. The steepest limit is `path`'s `rampMaxGrade` of 0.15 (V11 §3.24.5), on a lattice of about 25 m. So any lattice edge across a cliff, sheer or gorge face taller than about 3.75 m is impassable to every class, and F-ROUTE's last rung leaves the destination `unserved`. A mesa girt by such faces therefore gets no route in, against S3 (9)'s 'enter across the barriers'. EP-21 names 'a mesa town' as a B-EDGE fixture but gives no outcome that matches the generator. VPC-R1-02 (the wall grade of cliff-class arcs) is a different gap: its fix still leaves the sheer and gorge case, and any walled cliff-class mesa, to this rule.
issues.required_change: §4.2 S3 (9), the *Every arc closed* sentence: replace 'enter across the barriers' with 'enter across the barriers where §4.3's class grade limit admits an edge — a marsh, a cleft or ramp in a cliff, an island town's landings ((13)) — and otherwise take F-ROUTE's last rung (`unserved`, reported; §5.2), so a mesa girt by faces steeper than `path`'s `rampMaxGrade` over one lattice step has no road in at generation and says so'. Write the same outcome into EP-21's mesa fixture: 'every route in within its class grade, or `unserved` reported; 0 routes steeper than `path`'s limit'.

issues.claim: An `on_enceinte` castle × item 114's wall condition (walls × the castle at their limits; not in the catalogue). The castle's curtain is its own `Enceinte` of kind `bailey` (§2.7 `Castle.curtain`). Along `Castle.cityWeld` the bailey's outer arc and the town wall are 'one wall carrying both enceintes' `wall` roles' (§2.7; §4.8: 'the shared edge is one wall'). Each `Enceinte` carries its own `condition`, `conditionMaterial` and `conditionEpoch` profiles, and every writer works per enceinte: S7's generation row 'writes each run's `Enceinte.condition` and material' for every enceinte it furnishes, the bailey included (§4.8 *Condition at generation*; DR41: 'the enceintes and their stretches'); V06 §3.7.7 decays and repairs each ring on `stream(EVO_FORT, enceinte)` with its own local weight λ; `DeclineOp`'s `breach`/`dismantle` and `wearWall`/`repairWall` name one enceinte. No text says which profile governs the welded stretch. So the one wall is routinely `breached` on the town's profile and `standing` on the castle's, or patched in two materials. §8.2 then draws a whole wall line over a breach, and §11.1 exports the same edge as a wall and as an opening (a battle map's line of sight through a standing curtain). That is a silent contradictory result at TOWN and above wherever the castle sits on the wall and `walls.condition.atGeneration` is on, and at every epoch.
issues.required_change: §2.7, *An enceinte's condition by run*: add 'Along an `on_enceinte` castle's shared stretch (`Castle.cityWeld`) the town enceinte's three profiles are the stretch's one condition, material and epoch: the bailey's profiles there mirror them, written in the same batch by every writer — S7's generation row (one draw for the stretch, on the town enceinte), `DeclineOp`'s `breach` and `dismantle`, `wearWall`, `repairWall` and V06 §3.7.7's transitions, whichever of the two enceintes the op names — and never written apart.' §4.8 *Condition at generation* and V06 §3.7.7 (2)–(3) cite it (V06: the stretch decays and is repaired on the town ring's draws and λ). Add to §13.2's item-114 group a CITY fixture with an `on_enceinte` castle at a vulnerable, poor town's generation shares and over 10 epochs: the welded stretch's two profiles equal at every commit; §8.2 draws one state; §11.1's VTT gives one wall-or-opening answer per edge.

issues.claim: A raised way crossing a city wall × the round-1 support step (VEW-11 × VEW-12, both repairs). §2.7's support step (3) now makes 'an enceinte's wall strip (`Enceinte.strips`)' an obstacle that no pier may stand in. It also adds the clear-span bound: a merged clear span longer than `raisedWays.structure.maxClearSpanM` (masonry 30 m, timber 20 m; V11 §3.24.2) drops a generated course (`raised_too_long`) and bends a declared one. The only crossings of a wall allowed are 'on a gate's line or as the aqueduct's wall arch' (§4.3 *Where it may not go*; §4.13's wall row: '… no support in a wall strip'). The strips are band 2–3 m + inner setback 6–10 m + outer setback and glacis 10–20 m: 18–33 m (§4.8). With a moat it is band + inner setback + berm + the channel (c14 `era.moatWidthM` 8–16 m, c15 10–18 m), and the intervallum lane or a gate plaza is a further obstacle. So the span over a wall runs about 18–42 m. Every timber viaduct, and a large share of masonry aqueducts and viaducts, that must cross the wall is dropped. Two things then contradict it: §4.3, which carries a generated aqueduct 'crossing the wall through an arch', and V06 §3.7's raised gate, 'a gate whose tower carries the deck' — 'the deck's support' standing in the strip.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (3): add 'Where the course crosses an enceinte's trace — on a gate's line or as the aqueduct's wall arch (§4.3) — one station stands on the trace: the raised gate's tower (a viaduct or elevated road; V06 §3.7) or the curtain under the aqueduct's arch carries the deck there, its pier the wall's band (no footprint of its own); the strip's setback and glacis parts, the berm and the moat stay clear, and the clear-span bound reads the spans on either side of that station.' §4.13's wall cell reads 'no support in a wall strip but the crossing's station on the band'. V06 §3.7's 'a wall opening under an aqueduct is no support' is amended to match: the opening carries the span, and its stretch is taken as a raised gate's stretch is, after the aqueduct goes. T110-2 gains: a CITY masonry aqueduct across a moated c15 wall with an intervallum, and a timber viaduct on a gate's line — both built, 0 piers in a setback, glacis, berm or moat, every clear span ≤ its bound.

issues.claim: The intermediate terraces of §4.7 *Levelling and retaining walls* have no record and no datum. The repair (VEW-05) widened the rule: 'A step above `stepMaxCm` takes ⌈step ÷ `stepMaxCm`⌉ − 1 intermediate terraces, each at least `minTerraceDepthM` deep and each edge a wall of at most `stepMaxCm`, laid inside the two units'. The same applies to a levelled unit's edge against unlevelled ground. A levelled unit holds one datum (`Plot.platformCm`, `Block.platformCm`, §2.5), and 'the one reader of levelled heights', `levelledGroundCm`, returns 'the datum of the levelled plot, block or ward holding p'. A terrace laid inside a unit therefore has no height of its own anywhere. On both sides of an intermediate wall `levelledGroundCm` reads the same unit datum, so `stepProfile(wall)` derives a step of 0 for a wall raised to hold up to `stepMaxCm`. A building, V04 knot or shadow on the terrace reads the wrong level. EP-24's fixture 'a step above 2 × `stepMaxCm`' has no stated heights to check.
issues.required_change: §4.7 *Levelling*: state that an intermediate terrace splits the unit it is laid in along the contour into two levelling units, each with its own datum (as V07 §3.8a (2) splits a house platform: 'each levelled at its own datum, the footprints split with it by the base's stepped-wing rule'). For a plot, add a stepped datum to §2.5 — `Plot.platformSteps?: { line: ChainRef /* the intermediate wall */; datumCm: Cm }[]`, written by S11's levelling, in the plot's leaf digest; likewise `Block.platformSteps` for S10's — and have `levelledGroundCm` return the datum of the step region holding p. Add to EP-24 / B-EDGE: 'on a step of 2.5 × `stepMaxCm`, `levelledGroundCm` on each terrace equals its datum and every wall's `stepProfile` lies in (`stepMinCm`, `stepMaxCm`]'.

issues.claim: Item 116's zoom-out limit at the METROPOLIS cap. §8.8 defines k_min = max(0, k_fit − `view.zoomOutMarginStops`), with k_fit 'the largest k ≤ 34 with max(the bounds' width, height) ≤ the short side in CSS px × m_k'. The coarsest stop, k = 0, is m_0 ≈ 11.97 m per CSS px. The cap's frame is 17.53 km × 8.76 km (§3.2), so it fits only on a short side of at least ≈ 1 465 CSS px; the METROPOLIS target's 11.31 km needs ≈ 945. On a laptop or desktop window, and always on a phone, no k satisfies the test, so k_fit is undefined, and the max(0, …) clamp does not define it. T-ER-08's bar ('it stops at k_min, where the whole `bounds` fits the short side'), §9.5's *Fit the town* ('frames the whole `bounds` at the limit's stop') and item 116 (e)'s 'at every rung from THORP to the cap the zoom-out limit shows the whole bounds' cannot hold there. Item 116's §12.5 clause ('fewer stops, never more') forbids the obvious repair of adding coarser stops. Item 122 (i)'s widened limit, town plus camps, makes it larger still.
issues.required_change: §8.8: state the case. 'Where no stop k ≥ 0 fits — `bounds` wider than the short side × m_0 — k_fit is 0 and k_min is 0: the limit is the pyramid's coarsest stop, the view at it showing as much of `bounds` as fits, centred by §9.5's framing, the view status saying ‘the whole map is wider than this window’.' T-ER-08 and §9.5's *Fit* read 'the whole `bounds`, or stop 0 where it does not fit'. Add a METROPOLIS-cap fixture on a 900 × 1 600 and a 390 × 844 CSS-px viewport to T-ER-08. Because this narrows item 116 (e)'s bar at the cap, record it as a judgment row naming that clause. The alternative — stops below 0 for such maps — must be ruled against item 116's 'fewer stops, never more' before it is written.

issues.claim: A cliff inside a district × S8's bent-cut lanes (and V01's seeds, fans and lanes). The VEW-05 repair made such a cliff — an S1 `cliff` `SiteFeature` or ground over `walls.barriers`' `cliff` threshold — 'a hard line' for S10 and S11 only: no `RetainingWall`, no unit levelled across it, plots ending at the `cliff` setback from top and foot (§4.7). Nothing upstream of S10 reads it. S6 does not split districts or faces at it (§4.5). S8's recursive bent cut has only a slope term that turns the cut axis toward the contours (§4.6), and every intramural lane comes from S8's cuts (§4.4 S5c). So a cut, and the lane laid along it, can run straight down a cliff face that S10 refuses to plot. §4.3's class grade limit governs routed ways only, never S8's lanes. V01's fabrics read only a cliff that is a district's boundary run ('a hard `cliff` run', V01 §3.6 (7); V01 §3.18 (f)), never one inside the face. EP-24 names 'a cliff primitive across a district' but tests only the levelling cell. The outcome is a lane down a cliff, silently.
issues.required_change: §4.6 S8, the face preparation, before the first cut: 'each district face is split along every cliff inside it (an S1 `cliff` feature, or ground over `walls.barriers`' `cliff` threshold — §4.7's hard line), the split edge carrying the hard `cliff` role and no way, so no cut, lane, seed or plot crosses it; each side is cut as a face of its own, and V01's fabrics read the edge as V01 §3.6 (7)'s hard `cliff` run'. Point §4.7's *A cliff inside a district* at it. EP-24's 'cliff primitive across a district' fixture adds: '0 lanes, seeds or way spines crossing the cliff line; the two sides' plots backing onto it at the `cliff` setback'.

issues.claim: V04 §3.2 N7 (1) and N2 do not read the moat level §4.2 S3 (10) now derives. N7 says 'the terrain's height at the shore stands for the water surface, as §2.6's water table reads it, so the mouth sits `outfall.freeboardCm` above the water it discharges into'. The base, after its VEW-04 repair, says the moat's water level is one derived value — the `flowFrom` source's shore height — 'which every reader of the moat's water reads (… V04 §3.2 N2 and N7 …)', and the moat's banks stand up to `moat.maxFallCm` (400 cm) above it. On a moat outfall (N2's per-bank fallback) N7 therefore puts the mouth's floor up to 4 m above the moat's water, and the 'mouth sits `freeboardCm` above the water' rule (T-V4-2's 'every outfall invert ≥ the shore height + `freeboardCm`') is checked against the bank, not the water.
issues.required_change: V04 §3.2 N7 (1): 'Each outfall knot's floor is `low = s + freeboardCm`, `s` the receiving water's surface as §2.6's water table reads it — a moat's the derived level of §4.2 S3 (10), every other body's terrain height at the shore'. T-V4-2's outfall clause reads the same `s`; T-V4-80 (j)'s walled-core-in-a-wet-moat fixture adds a moat on sloping ground.
